threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Overground' instead of 'the Ginger Line.' That's a surefire sign you’re new to Dalston.
Caught a group of teens on the 36 last night, passionately debating whether pineapple belongs on pizza. Didn't even notice the drunk guy snoring next to them.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a flock of chickens roaming free in a backyard while the owner sipped coffee, I knew this place was different.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Neukölln can you grab a late-night Döner and watch a rooftop movie under the stars, all while hearing live jazz from the street below.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone is local if they still call it the 'BART station' instead of just 'Civic Center.' It’s the small things that give it away.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a guy in a gorilla suit boarded my bus at 5th Street. He handed out bananas while singing 'I Want It That Way.' Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that the best vermut is served in tiny bars with no sign; the real charm is in the hidden corners, not the crowded plazas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the packed terrace at 10 PM; it’s a rite of passage here to know that’s just the start.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver yells, 'Last stop!' while the rest of us grab our bags and head for the door.
Saw a bloke on the 59 last night trying to impress a girl with a magic trick, ended up spilling his drink all over her lap instead.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I spotted a family of raccoons raiding the bakery's trash at dawn, nonchalantly strolling down the street like they owned the place.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you have a techno party in an abandoned factory, then grab a döner from a food truck that plays live DJ sets. It’s a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You spot a true local if they still know where the legendary pink church used to be—nothing else has changed around here since the '90s.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a woman knitting on the T while a guy tap danced for tips. Only in SF does a yarn and rhythm combo unfold mid-commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think cafés in Gràcia are all about brunch and selfies, but locals know the best croissants are hidden in the back of a tiny bakery on Carrer de Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they mistakenly ask for 'tapas' in a café instead of 'pintxos' when they're in Gràcia.
